C-41.IntentSummary: T1: ship Paper and Ink as new themes and the defaults for new installs, and replace the title-bar light/dark toggle with an Auto → Light → Dark button (Avenex icons). T2 (family model, picker by family, migrations) and T3 (six new members, contrast pass) planned 2026-10-15 after the family list was confirmed; delegated to two ZCode agents in parallel worktrees, merged by the orchestrator.

T-001.Title: Paper + Ink themes as defaults; Auto/Light/Dark title-bar button

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: paper.theme.css and ink.theme.css added (from the reviewed drafts), registered like every other theme (themeMap, theme lists, dark-theme classification for ink), selectable in Settings, with names in every locale.
New installs default to followSystemTheme=true, lightModeTheme=paper, darkModeTheme=ink; existing users keep their stored theme.

Title-bar theme button cycles Auto → Light → Dark with the Avenex icons and a localized tooltip; Auto sets followSystemTheme and follows prefers-color-scheme changes live; Light/Dark pick lightModeTheme/darkModeTheme.
Unit tests: cycle order, Auto resolution for both OS appearances, live appearance change, defaults for a fresh profile, stored theme preserved.

T-002.Title: Family model: 14 light/dark families, picker by family, removed themes migrate

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: config.js exports one frozen THEME_FAMILIES list (id, name, light, dark) for the 14 families of spec R-3, in that order; themePairs is derived from it (each member maps to its partner) so every existing pair consumer keeps working.

The 13 dropped ids are removed from themeMap, themeColor.js, railscastsThemes, the theme CSS files (and prismjs/export companions if a dropped theme has its own), commands/index.js, the native View › Theme menu (m009_menu.rs) and the Settings picker; menu-consistency stays green.

Migration map (one exported constant, applied when stored preferences load, to theme, lightModeTheme and darkModeTheme): light→paper, dark→ink, rose-pine-moon→rose-pine, tokyo-night-storm→tokyo-night, ayu-mirage→ayu-dark, monokai-pro→one-dark, material-dark→one-dark, nightfox→nord, palenight→catppuccin-mocha, horizon-dark→rose-pine, synthwave-84→dracula, cyberdream→tokyo-night, oxocarbon-dark→graphite-dark. Any other unknown id falls back to paper (light) / ink (dark). Valid stored ids are never rewritten. The migrated value is persisted once.

Settings theme page shows families (one swatch pair per family, light and dark halves); choosing a family sets lightModeTheme and darkModeTheme to its members and theme to the member for the current mode (Auto: system appearance; Light/Dark: that member). The title-bar button keeps cycling Auto → Light → Dark within the chosen family.

Unit tests: every family has a registered light and dark member; every dropped id migrates per the map for all three keys; unknown id fallback; valid id untouched; picking a family in each mode; themePairs symmetric.

T-003.Title: Six new family members and a contrast pass over all 28 themes

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: New themes one-light, alucard, nord-light, kanagawa-lotus, graphite-dark, ulysses-dark, built on the Paper/Ink structure (same variable set), using each family's published palette (Atom One Light, Dracula Alucard, Nord Snow Storm, Kanagawa Lotus); Graphite Dark and Ulysses Dark derived from their light members. Registered in themeMap, themeColor.js, dark classification (graphite-dark, ulysses-dark), commands, the native menu and every locale (product names, untranslated).

A contrast test reads every shipped *.theme.css and asserts WCAG AA (4.5:1) for body text on the editor background and for link colour, and 3:1 for muted/secondary text; themes that fail are fixed by adjusting colours, not by excluding them.
Every theme defines the same variable set as Paper (a test lists missing variables per theme).
